title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000028: two security requirements set a zero-false-rejection acceptance criterion that no correct implementation can meet, so no verification measure against them can ever pass

standards_mappings.rationale: Problem resolution management: a material contradiction becomes a recorded problem, not a silent edit.
The obligation to record rather than to conceal.

lifecycle_status_note: reviewed: the subject record(s) named by this finding were corrected at source in a separate, controlled remediation pass, each with its revision incremented and a revision_history entry appended, and the correction was verified by re-running the corpus validator, the toolchain self-tests and the acceptance suite. revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Replaced the unsatisfiable zero-false-rejection acceptance criterion in FB2-SAF-SEC-000003 and FB2-SAF-SEC-000004 (both revision 1 -> 2) with a rate bound of 1 per 10^6 genuine frames, a required demonstration population of at least 3 x 10^6, and a minimum integrity value width of 22 bits; regenerated FB2-VER-TMS-000018/19 and FB2-VER-EXE-000018/19 against it. Left every countable, non-collision-prone zero in both records unchanged.

evidence: FB2-SAF-SEC-000003's criterion 'Genuine-frame false-rejection rate, Genuine frames rejected under nominal bus conditions over 24 h, 0, frames' and FB2-SAF-SEC-000004's 'Genuine-frame false-rejection rate, Genuine frames rejected over 24 h at nominal bus load, 0, frames' are both absolute zeros over a finite window on a channel that carries an integrity value. An integrity value of any practical width collides with some payload: the acceptance criterion is therefore unachievable by a correct implementation and achievable only by one that never rejects anything, which would also satisfy the requirement's other criteria vacuously. The same pattern appears in FB2-SAF-SEC-000001's 'Plaintext bytes recoverable ... 0 bytes' and FB2-SAF-SEC-000002's 'Connections ... refused ... 0 connections', which are zeros over a countable event rather than over a collision-prone channel and are therefore achievable; the distinction matters and the two requirements do not make it.
impact: A requirement with an unachievable acceptance criterion cannot be verified, and a verification measure written against it has no possible pass. That is exactly what this pass found while authoring FB2-VER-TMS-000018 and FB2-VER-TMS-000019: the honest thing to do was record the requirement's own zero as the expected outcome and state on the face of the measure that a real implementation would need a rate threshold with a stated bound. Both measures carry that statement in their oracle_detail. A reviewer who ran them would find an unpassable measure and would be right to.
root_cause: The criteria were written as absolutes because a security requirement is easier to state as 'nothing gets through' than as 'no more than N per million frames at 99.9 percent confidence'. The convenience form is unfalsifiable, which makes it read as strictness and is in fact the opposite: a criterion nobody can meet cannot distinguish a good implementation from a bad one.
resolution: RESOLVED at source, in the requirement rather than in the test measure, which is the correct place: a criterion no correct implementation can meet is a requirement defect. FB2-SAF-SEC-000003's 'Genuine-frame false-rejection rate' criterion was changed from an absolute '0 frames over 24 h' to a bounded rate of 1 rejection per 10^6 genuine frames, demonstrated as 0 rejections over a genuine-frame population of at least 3 x 10^6 in a 24 h campaign, together with a new requirement that the integrity value on the interface be at least 22 bits. FB2-SAF-SEC-000004 received the identical criterion. Both records moved to revision 2. The arithmetic: a keyed integrity value of width w rejects a genuine frame with probability 2^-w, so over a 24 h campaign the expected number of genuine rejections is n * 2^-w, which is non-zero for any practical w - which is why the zero was unachievable. 0 failures in n trials gives a one-sided 95 percent upper confidence bound of 3/n, so 3/n <= 1e-6 requires n >= 3e6, which is where the population comes from. Sustaining a rate at or below 1e-6 across 3e6 frames needs a per-frame probability at or below 3.3e-7, i.e. 2^-w <= 3.3e-7, i.e. w >= 22 bits, which is where the width comes from. The replacement is therefore not a relaxation: it is STRICTER in discriminating power than the zero it replaces, because an always-rejecting implementation scores about 100 percent and fails it by four orders of magnitude, and a 16-bit integrity value gives about 1.5e-5 per frame and also fails it, whereas both would have satisfied the old zero. It is also a harder engineering obligation, because it constrains the width of the integrity value where the zero constrained nothing. The absolute zeros that REMAIN in both records are the ones that are decidable by the check existing - injected frames accepted, replayed frames accepted, length-mismatch frames reaching the callback, unframed bytes passing, control-byte transitions - and those are over countable events on a channel where no collision is involved, so they were deliberately NOT relaxed; the finding itself made this distinction and it was preserved. Dependents regenerated: FB2-VER-TMS-000018 and FB2-VER-TMS-000019 (both revision 1 -> 2) now record the population, the rate bound and the width as expected outcomes and no longer describe the criterion as unachievable; FB2-VER-EXE-000018 and FB2-VER-EXE-000019 (both revision 1 -> 2) no longer list a decision on the criterion as a blocker - it is no longer a decision the project owes - and instead list the engineering prerequisites the revised criterion creates. Both execution records remain execution_kind 'none' and outcome 'blocked': no bus was instrumented, no frame was injected, and nothing in this revision claims that either requirement has been verified. Findings FB2-REV-FND-000008..000012 remain OPEN, because those ask for verification evidence and none exists. Human approval remains pending for every record named here: no human has confirmed this correction, no tool has been qualified, no certification is claimed and no ASPICE capability level is claimed. production_authorized stays false and product_verification_credit stays false on every record touched.
